Ana (CSE): Heads-up — customer ACMEInc (ticket #9842) sees users created via SCIM but getting default role 'viewer' instead of 'admin' after a group rename in their IdP earlier today. They say it worked yesterday.
Ana (CSE): Primary symptom: group-to-role mapping didn't match, so mapping fallback applied. Also seeing intermittent 403s for group PATCH calls right after the rename.
Ana (CSE): Pasted the relevant log snippet from our provisioning worker: 
```
2026-02-12T14:03:31.123Z WARN scim-provisioner PATCH /Groups/12ab34cd status=403 body={"error":"insufficient_scope","error_description":"Token lacks: scim:groups:write"}
2026-02-12T14:03:31.124Z INFO scim-provisioner user=joe@example.com created role=viewer source=group-fallback
```

Mike (SRE): Can you confirm this is the OAuth token we store for the IdP sync? Last rotation was 2026-01-28. Also any change to the IdP group externalId vs displayName? Those bite us sometimes.
Ana (CSE): Confirmed: IdP admin reported they renamed group from 'ACME Admins' -> 'ACME_Admins' (underscore). Prior mapping used exact match on displayName. Our mapping config uses displayName by default.
Jess (PM): So two things: 1) mismatch due to case/char change -> mapping missed. 2) 403 suggests token scope problem when we tried to patch group metadata. Could be a separate failure during resync.
Sam (Eng): Repro steps I ran on staging: created group with displayName 'test-admin', mapped role admin, then changed displayName to 'test_admin' in IdP. Our sync created group but mapping didn't apply because our matcher is exact. Replicated the 403 by using a token lacking the groups:write scope. Repro commands below.
```
# simulate PATCH that fails due to scope
curl -i -X PATCH \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_WITHOUT_GROUPS_WRITE" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/scim/v2/Groups/12ab34cd \
  -d '{"displayName":"ACME_Admins"}'
# response -> 403 {"error":"insufficient_scope"}
```

Sam (Eng): SCIM payload we expect from IdP when renaming (example):
```
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group"],
  "id": "12ab34cd",
  "displayName": "ACME_Admins",
  "members": [{"value":"u-123","display":"joe@example.com"}]
}
```

Ana (CSE): Customer says their SCIM app uses a token with scopes: ['scim:read','scim:write'] per IdP console. They claim no groups:write separate scope. But logs show missing 'scim:groups:write'.
Mike (SRE): We need to check our token scope parsing + mapping to internal permission names. It might be that some IdPs have a single 'scim:write' while our checks expect granular 'scim:groups:write'. If the check is too strict, we should accept superset tokens.
Sam (Eng): Agreed. Quick mitigation: update our sync worker to fallback: if PATCH returns 403 and token has any scim:*write scope, retry a GET-then-recreate flow that uses endpoints permitted by current scopes. That avoids blocking deprovision/provision loops. I'll sketch a patch.
Jess (PM): Also product question: should mapping be case-insensitive and tolerant to common punctuation? We should avoid exact match brittleness. Propose normalized matching (lowercase, strip spaces/_/-.).
Ana (CSE): Customer ok with a manual re-sync after we patch. They asked for an audit of who changed the group in IdP (they have logs and will share).
Sam (Eng): Action items I'm taking:
- Fix scope check to accept broader 'scim:write' variants or map provider scopes. (PR in progress)
- Add a retry path for 403 on group PATCH that uses fallback flow.
- Add normalized matching for group displayName -> mapping rules (opt-in for now).
- Add a one-off admin endpoint to trigger re-eval of group mappings per tenant.

Mike (SRE): I'll rotate the stored token for ACMEInc and try a resync after Sam's patch lands. If rotation fails, will revert to manual mapping change for affected users.
scim-bot: Scheduled job 'tenant-resync/ACMEInc' queued at 2026-02-12T15:00:00Z by Mike (SRE).
Ana (CSE): Customer updated: they ran an IdP-initiated re-sync and saw a few 403s, then reverted rename temporarily so access restored. They're OK with a maintenance window to apply changes.
Jess (PM): We'll aim to ship minimal fix (scope acceptance + fallback retry) in next patch release (v0.82.1) and follow-up with normalized matching in v0.83.0. Sam, can you include migration plan in PR?
Sam (Eng): Yep. PR will include migration steps and a one-time job to re-evaluate mappings for tenants who opted in. ETA: EOD tomorrow for hotfix, normalized matching next sprint.
Ana (CSE): I'll coordinate maintenance window with ACMEInc and confirm they can re-run after patch.
Mike (SRE): After hotfix, I'll run a repro: rename group -> observe provisioning -> check roles assigned. Will paste logs here.
Ana (CSE): Thanks all — marking ticket #9842 as 'escalated' and will update customer after hotfix validation. :thumbsup:
